title: A schema-rejected StructuredOutput invocation can be corrected before the exact terminal completes

evidence.note: The live kimi-k3 turn first invoked StructuredOutput without the required kind field. Claude Code returned an explicit schema-error tool result. The provider then reused the completed native id with the exact four-field terminal object, received a successful tool result, and emitted the same exact final structured_output. The Lab nevertheless faulted on the first invocation before reading its error result and later recovery.

observation: The parser validated terminal-tool arguments at invocation time and declared any terminal-tool error fatal. That loses the CLI's own closed-schema recovery lifecycle. The stream is unambiguous when the malformed invocation receives an error result, a later invocation receives success with the exact expected object, and the final terminal repeats that object. Accepting an error without a later exact success would weaken completion and remains invalid.
proposed_change: Defer StructuredOutput argument validation until its tool result. Record schema-rejected invocations as error_recovered only when a later exact StructuredOutput invocation completes successfully and the final structured_output remains identical. Continue refusing malformed successful invocations, unpaired results, overlapping ids, an unrecovered terminal error, or any final-terminal mismatch.
verification_plan: Replay the retained softplus_gradient stream, exercise recovered and unrecovered terminal sequences in the contract suite, publish an Executor successor, then rerun softplus_gradient in a fresh workspace.
